summary:
Specs for 49 actuators, checked 2026-11-07, from manufacturer datasheets, parameter sheets, drawings and official stores, plus distributors for some prices. Main findings:

(1) The incumbent RMD-X4-P36-36-E (V4) only partly matches the project notes. 360 g, Ø55 x 61 mm (the 61 mm includes a 3 mm Ø35 output pilot) and 10.5 N·m at 83 rpm at 24 V all hold. But peak torque is 34 N·m, not 30, and the module Kt is 1.9 N·m/A, not 1.8. The 30 N·m peak (with 36 N·m stall), the 1.8 N·m/A(rms) and the 0.4 Ω all belong to the newer V4.1 variant RMD-X4-P36-36-E-L, so the notes seem to mix the two variants. The 0.39-0.4 Ω is a line-to-line value, so the per-phase figure is about 0.2 Ω, not 0.4. MyActuator's own sources also disagree with each other on this (0.35, 0.39 and 0.4 Ω), and on inductance, pole pairs and backlash.

(2) MyActuator's 'rated' torque is not a continuous thermal rating. The V4.1 spec sheets define it as a duty cycle (90-degree swings with 5 s holds) and include temperature-rise tables. In those tables the motor reaches thermal equilibrium at only about 50-80 % of the rated figure, and less at rated speed: X4-36-L 7.5-8.5 vs 10.5 N·m; X6-50-L 9-13 vs 20; X8-150 20-38 vs 43; X10-200 43-55 vs 60; X4-10-L 2.0-2.9 vs 4. At the rated torque the winding reaches 100 °C in roughly 2-60 minutes depending on model and speed. In V4.1 model names the number is the stall torque; peak torque is defined at 10 rpm and is lower. Older V2/V3 MyActuator units use a different rating: 24 °C ambient with a 60 °C temperature rise at equilibrium.

(3) CubeMars does not publish the test condition behind its rated torque. Its product pages give the motor-side KT and line-to-line resistance. The headline price is the 'Driver Board: NO' option; the 'YES' option costs $36-100 more. The ledger price is the YES price; confirm with CubeMars what the NO option ships with.

(4) Every Unitree motor is RS-485 only, not CAN: GO-M8010-6, A1, B1-16, IM6014 and the J288 servo. They would need a CAN-to-RS-485 bridge. The B1 motor shows as unavailable in the store.

(5) RobStride is cheapest per newton-metre. RS04 gives 120 N·m peak / 40 N·m rated at 1.42 kg for $255; RS03 gives 60 N·m peak / 20 N·m rated at 0.88 kg for $225. Backlash and drawings are not published.

(6) MyActuator X6-40, X8-25 (the former 'X8 Pro'), X10-100 and the V4 X4-10 are discontinued. X8-60 and X8-90 are not on the current MyActuator site.

(7) Expression servos publish no continuous torque rating. ROBOTIS gives stall torque only and says it differs from continuous output. Feetech gives a 'rated torque', but the 12 V 30 kg·cm STS3215 is the C018/C047 variant; the 7.4 V C001 stalls at only 1.6-1.9 N·m.

Torque constants are output-side except CubeMars, whose motor-side values are marked 'Kt side' in the notes. Where a vendor gives line-to-line resistance, phase_resistance_ohm holds the Y-equivalent value (line-to-line divided by 2), and the original is in the notes. Unit conversions used: 1 kg·cm = 0.0980665 N·m; 1 rad/s = 9.549 rpm; 1 degree = 60 arcmin.

CubeMars: no published rated-torque/thermal test definition found on product pages, the AK V3 software manual, AK module product manual v3.0.0 or driver manuals; temperature-rise curves are images only. AK60-6 V3 and AK10-9 V3 pages list no backlash.
CubeMars 'Driver Board YES/NO' meaning not documented on the page (product text says the driver is integrated); prices obtained via the store's own price endpoint goods.php?act=price.

RobStride: site is a JS single-page app; specs/prices read from the official bundle https://robstride.com/assets/index-957329aa.js. No backlash, drawings, Max-Overload chart data or RS10P dimensions found.
Unitree A1 motor and B1-16: gear ratio, dimensions and rated torque not on official pages; Unitree shop shows 'Unitree B1 Motor' $3000 with available=false.
Unitree IM6014: no nominal voltage stated (curve at 60 V; input 24-75 V).
ROBOTIS e-Manual publishes no continuous/rated torque for XM/XH series (stall torque only).

Feetech official site (feetechrc.com) intermittently reset connections (needed retries) and publishes no prices; STS3250 USD price only from OpenELAB (C002 variant); no reputable US distributor price found for STS3250-C001.
MyActuator X8-32 V4-manual drawing dimensions did not extract (font issue) and were not rendered; diameter/length left null.

actuators.notes: Check against the project notes: 360 g correct. Ø55 x 61 mm correct (61 includes 3 mm pilot). 10.5 N·m at 83 rpm at 24 V correct as a vendor 'rated' value. 30 N·m peak WRONG for -E (V4 manual and US store both say 34 N·m; 30 N·m peak / 36 N·m stall is the V4.1 -E-L). 1.8 N·m/A WRONG for -E (module Kt 1.9 N·m/A; 1.8 N·m/A(rms) is the -E-L). '~0.4 ohm/phase' is a line-to-line figure: the manual gives 'Line Resistance' 0.39 Ω with Y wiring, so phase_resistance_ohm holds the Y-equivalent 0.39/2. A copper-loss check on the sibling X8-120 and X12-320 shows the vendor value cannot be per-phase. Official sources conflict: the US page and User Manual V1.1 (2025-05-16) give 0.35 Ω, 0.17 mH, 13 pole pairs and 10 arcmin; the 2026-10-29 V4 manual (used here) gives 0.39 Ω, 0.07 mH, 11 pole pairs and <=15 arcmin. Kt side: output ('Module Torque Constant'); currents are phase A(rms). Also from the manual: efficiency 63.1 %, back-EMF 6 Vdc/krpm, backdrive torque 1.14 N·m, crossed-roller bearing (1.3 kN axial, 1.5 kN radial), 0.3 kg·cm². The motor label in the manual photo reads '100W 12N.m 83rpm 1:36', not 10.5 N·m - unexplained.
